criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The need for reef monitoring and its benefit to marine and conservation scientists are clear, and the report identifies useful mission functions. However, objectives remain broad: it does not establish specific mission requirements, instrument capabilities, coverage, or performance targets.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A timetable is provided with accompanying task descriptions, and relevant information sources and STK work are identified. The schedule is plausible but lacks contingency provision and detail on how choices will be evaluated or adjusted; its link to the mission is present but not developed into a tailored design plan.

evidence.quote: The goal is to brainstorm and research as many possible strategies for the satellite’s launch/orbit

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: The report demonstrates background research and software familiarisation, but presents no preliminary calculations, orbit or launch analysis, simulations, or interpreted technical results. This is useful preparation, but not sufficient technical progress for the criterion.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings and a readable, labelled Gantt chart make the report easy to navigate. The writing is generally understandable, but includes some informal phrasing and grammatical awkwardness. Sources are provided, though reference presentation is informal and not consistently bibliographic.

evidence.quote: The final report is due on 20/11/20 at 5pm.

technical_issues.issue: The proposed seafloor colour/tone method is not translated into an instrument design or feasibility assessment; spectral bands, spatial resolution, water depth, turbidity, and atmospheric effects are unaddressed.
Near-real-time monitoring is not supported by an orbit/revisit analysis, communications or downlink concept, or latency requirements.
“30 percent more acidic” is imprecise: ocean acidification is commonly described as about a 30% increase in hydrogen-ion concentration, corresponding to a pH decrease, rather than a 30% change in pH.
No preliminary launch/orbit calculations or STK outputs are presented, so the mission’s technical feasibility and progress cannot yet be assessed.

overall: The mission rationale, timetable, and source list are clear, but technical progress is limited to research and tutorials. Criterion marks are 6/10, 6/10, 3/10, and 6/10 (approximately 57/100 when weighted).

feedback.summary: You present a clear reef-monitoring rationale, a readable timetable in Image 1, and relevant sources in “Useful Links.” To strengthen the report, turn the broad mission functions into measurable design requirements, add interpreted technical results, and develop the plan and presentation to a more professional, mission-specific level.
next_steps: In “Mission Concept & Rationale,” define measurable coverage and performance requirements, then assess whether a proposed instrument can meet them, including spectral bands, resolution, water depth and turbidity. Clarify the acidification statistic: describe the change in hydrogen-ion concentration and corresponding pH decrease.

Move beyond research and STK tutorials in “Project Plan & Preliminary Progress”: include preliminary launch or orbit calculations, STK outputs and brief interpretations. To support near-real-time monitoring, analyse revisit, communications/downlink and latency requirements.

Build on Image 1 with contingency tasks and explain how the schedule’s design choices serve the reef-monitoring mission. For the next presentation level, use consistent bibliographic references and formal, grammatically polished writing throughout.

criteria.C1: “Mission Concept & Rationale” clearly identifies reef monitoring’s users and benefits, including marine and conservation scientists. To reach Accomplished, define specific mission requirements and show how instrument capabilities, coverage and performance targets meet those needs. Also assess the proposed seafloor colour/tone method and describe ocean acidification precisely as increased hydrogen-ion concentration with a corresponding pH decrease.
criteria.C2: Image 1 and the task descriptions provide a plausible timetable, and “Useful Links” identifies relevant sources. To reach Accomplished, add contingency provision and explain how the plan is tailored to the mission and how design choices will be evaluated or adjusted. Include the orbit/revisit, downlink and latency work needed to support the proposed near-real-time service.
criteria.C3: Your background research and completion of STK tutorials 1–4 show preparation. However, no preliminary calculations, launch/orbit analysis, simulations or interpreted technical results are presented. To progress, include useful technical work; the Accomplished level requires preliminary results with brief description or interpretation that demonstrate the project is on track.
criteria.C4: The report has clear headings, and Image 1 is a labelled, readable Gantt chart. To reach Accomplished, refine informal or awkward phrasing and make reference presentation consistent and properly bibliographic, ensuring citations in the text match the reference list. Maintain clear, consistent formatting for all figures and tables.
